name: Teal Starr
life: “I still remember signing expenses a worker felt guilty submitting.” On Tuesday, near Tideline Market, Teal picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I did her payroll. The route took an extra fifteen minutes every Friday and she never asked me to find them.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a faded indigo overshirt and a thin silver ring worn on a cord. Teal has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with short copper curls. Teal starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Teal treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Teal lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To account for the Friday quarter-hours.
family: Elinor Stein is Teal’s second cousin. Teal brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Elinor checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *A boat for sale twice*, Elinor says, “I only wanted the dinghy we learned to row in.”
connections: Jody Schmidt. A payroll worker records the lost quarter hours and a neighbor supplies the first dark-morning lift.
